chunks: My father - may God be pleased with him - said in his letter to me: Indeed, from the Sunnah is the attentiveness (turning the heart) in six prayers.

They are: the first unit of the night prayer; the single unit of the Witr prayer; the first of the two units of the midday (Zawal) prayer; the first unit of the two units of Ihram (prayer of entering Islam); the first unit of the supererogatory prayers of Maghrib; and the first unit of the obligatory prayer.

key_terms.التَّوَجُّهَ: Attentiveness / Turning the heart towards God
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْ الْإِحْرَامِ: The two units of Ihram prayer (prayed upon entering Islam)

ai.seo_question: Which six prayers require special attentiveness at their beginning according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), transmitted via his father, establishes the Sunnah of cultivating deep attentiveness (khushu') at the onset of six specific prayers, highlighting the spiritual significance of the initial moments of worship. This practice underscores the Shia emphasis on quality over mere quantity in prayer, ensuring the believer enters the state of divine connection immediately. The selection of these specific prayers reflects a holistic approach to maintaining spiritual mindfulness throughout the day's various obligatory and supererogatory acts.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 6-32 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - in what he wrote to me emphasized that attentiveness at the beginning of six prayers is recommendable.

They are the first unit of the night prayer; one unit of Al-Vatr prayer ; the first unit of the noon’s supererogatory prayer; the first unit of the Ihram prayer; the first unit of the evening supererogatory prayers; and the first unit of the obligatory prayers.”
